key_insight: SpatialClaw argues that better spatial reasoning in VLM agents depends not just on stronger perception tools, but on a better action interface for how those tools are called. The paper reframes the problem as an interaction-design issue: the agent’s interface can either unlock or limit open-ended spatial reasoning.
problem_solved: This paper addresses the challenge of enabling vision-language models to reliably reason about 3D spatial relationships, object locations, and motion using external perception tools. It specifically investigates why current tool-augmented agents struggle when the action interface is too restrictive or poorly designed.
method: Studies the action interface as the key bottleneck in tool-augmented spatial reasoning agents.
Introduces SpatialClaw as a rethought interface for invoking specialist perception modules in a more flexible, agentic way.
Evaluates how interface design affects open-ended spatial reasoning performance in VLM-based agents.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work highlights that improving agent performance may require redesigning the tool-use interface, not just adding more powerful models or detectors. It offers a practical lens for building more capable spatially aware agents in robotics, embodied AI, and multimodal reasoning systems.

paper_title: SpatialClaw: Rethinking Action Interface for Agentic Spatial Reasoning
paper_authors: Seokju Cho, Ryo Hachiuma, Abhishek Badki, Hang Su, Byung-Kwan Lee
